title: Inducare Pharma Faces Fresh Licence Cancellation Over Substandard Drugs, Metronidazole Violations

thbAction: Use the article as an entry point to pitch THB's commercial visibility layer for territory planning, account prioritization, and next-best-action for pharma leadership teams.
contentHtml:
Pune: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Pune division, has once again cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation, located in Purandar, Pune district, following serious violations involving the manufacture and distribution of substandard, misbranded and spurious drugs.

According to a recent media report in The Indian Express, the action was taken on November 23, with the company directed to immediately stop all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

The regulatory action involves the cancellation of the firm's Form 25 and Form 28 manufacturing licences. Form 25 licences cover the manufacture of general pharmaceutical products, including tablets, capsules, syrups and ointments, while Form 28 licences cover biological and special-category products such as vaccines, sera, blood products and sterile preparations.

According to Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, serious irregularities were identified during a joint inspection of the manufacturing facility conducted in July 2026. The inspection report documented 25 major deficiencies related to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), which prescribe standards to ensure the consistent quality, safety and efficacy of pharmaceutical products. Following the inspection, statutory samples of various medicines manufactured by the firm were sent to government analysts in Mumbai and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for testing.

The FDA had initially cancelled the company's manufacturing licences on September 7, 2026, after detecting large-scale production without proper batch manufacturing records. Investigators found that the firm had procured more than 550 kg of Metronidazole IP, an antibiotic, without maintaining records documenting its utilisation. The company had also manufactured approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of CAREGYL-400 (Batch No. IT6050) without the required test reports, of which around 5.2 lakh tablets had already been distributed.

Government analysis of the CAREGYL-400 batch revealed that the tablets contained only 32.44 per cent of the prescribed quantity of Metronidazole, resulting in the product being classified as Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). The inspection also revealed discrepancies in the manufacturing dates of Ciprofloxacin tablets produced in March 2026, which carried a manufacturing date of December 2025.

Further violations included the absence of records for in-process quality checks and the destruction of rejected and expired materials. The firm had also supplied medicines to a Pune-based distributor on 28 occasions between July 2025 and June 2026 without maintaining or issuing the mandatory reports. Inspectors additionally reported poor housekeeping conditions at the manufacturing premises, including cobwebs, unclean changing rooms and finished pharmaceutical products stored directly on the floor without adequate temperature and humidity monitoring.

The FDA also found that the manufacturer had produced and marketed nine pharmaceutical products without obtaining the necessary product permissions. In its written response, the firm reportedly acknowledged that separate product permissions had not been obtained for these medicines. Following laboratory analysis, government analysts declared all nine products either Not of Standard Quality, misbranded or spurious.

Among the serious findings, Ibucare Plus tablets containing Ibuprofen 400 mg and Paracetamol 325 mg were found to contain no Ibuprofen. Based on the test results, government analysts classified the medicine as spurious. FDA officials also highlighted concerns involving medicines commonly prescribed for patients with heart disease, hypertension, diabetes and digestive disorders. They warned that medicines containing no active pharmaceutical ingredient or substantially lower quantities than prescribed could result in treatment failure and pose serious risks to patients.

After the initial cancellation, the FDA issued a show-cause notice to the firm on October 29, 2026, and conducted a personal hearing on November 23. However, the Licensing Authority rejected the firm's defence that no complaints had been received from patients. FDA officials maintained that the absence of patient complaints did not eliminate the potential risks associated with spurious and substandard medicines.

Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe emphasised that ensuring the availability of safe, effective and quality medicines remains a primary responsibility of the regulatory authority. He further stated that strict regulatory and legal action would be taken against manufacturers involved in producing medicines without the required product permissions or compromising public health.

The Indian Express reports that the latest action follows multiple findings of manufacturing and quality-control violations at the firm's Pune facility, including the production of medicines without product permissions and the distribution of products that failed to meet prescribed quality standards.

The FDA has directed Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation to discontinue all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution operations following the cancellation of its Form 25 and Form 28 licences, while also proposing prosecution under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
